A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Affostruction. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, references, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated qualitative examples and retained ablations.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction and affordance-grounding results in Tables 1–3, multi-view and active-view experiments, and a sampling-step ablation in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds runtime/memory measurements, multi-object grounding examples, and failure cases in Section 4.5.

M1.justification: v2 adds a multi-object inference adaptation: SAM3D reconstructs and segments objects before affordance grounding is applied independently to each object. The core sparse voxel fusion, flow models, losses, and active-view selection procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Figure 6 adds a qualitative multi-object scene scenario beyond the object-centric evaluations in v1. The principal training datasets and benchmark coverage remain. Toys4k becoming Toky4K does not establish a different dataset: the description, 1,250-sample count, and displayed identifiers in Table A3 match.

E2.justification: The named comparator sets are retained, and the new runtime comparison reuses existing pipelines. However, PointRefer retains its labels and scores while its citation changes from Nguyen et al.'s Language-conditioned affordance-pose detection to Li et al.'s LASO. The PDFs do not resolve whether this is an attribution correction or a comparator change.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported training budget from 450K to 1M steps, a substantial increase, although v2 Appendix A.2 still specifies 450K; actual retraining is not established. v2 also designates aIoU as the primary grounding metric and introduces a separate runtime/memory evaluation on one RTX A6000.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 adds computational-efficiency analysis, a multi-object case study, and explicit failure cases testing reconstruction error propagation and misleading initial affordance estimates. Conversely, v1's four-sample demonstration of same-query affordance diversity is removed. The multi-view, active-selection, and appendix sampling-step ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Generative sampling steps and the qualitative diversity demonstration do not constitute statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes Shap-E's PSNR/LPIPS from 16.59/0.2989 to 13.07/0.4358 and InstantMesh's from 19.57/0.2382 to 16.59/0.2989, making the unchanged Affostruction PSNR of 18.84 the highest reported. New Table 4 reports total runtimes of 7.20, 8.30, and 35.37 seconds for Affostruction, TRELLIS+Espresso-3D, and MCC+Espresso-3D, alongside memory measurements. New scene and failure findings broaden the results; Tables 2–3 and retained ablation curves remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 retain the same objectives, conditioning, view-selection score, and affordance metrics. Changes to voxel-count symbols and feature indexing are not substantive mathematical revisions. Neither version adds theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The three central contributions and headline 19.1 aIoU and 32.67 IoU results remain. v2 foregrounds orientation alignment and limited-view efficiency, and highlights a 54.8% reconstruction advantage over the strongest baseline instead of v1's abstract-level 67.7%. Its introduction also inconsistently attributes the reconstruction result to Affogato, whereas Table 1 identifies the toy benchmark.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges reconstruction errors propagating into grounding and incorrect predictions misleading view selection, qualifying v1's optimistic account of overcoming decoupled-pipeline limitations. It adds object-centric and SAM3D multi-view limitations, explains the aIoU/MAE tradeoff through standard versus focal BCE, and interprets partial-grounding performance against the strongest MCC+Espresso-3D baseline.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link, clarifies stage-specific training data, identifies the active-view experiment's Furnitures subset, and supplies runtime hardware and MCC query-chunk details. Architectural tables and most appendix hyperparameters remain unchanged. The conflicting 1M and 450K training statements reduce reproducibility clarity.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including 3DTopia-XL, Gibson, SAM3D, FixMatch, FlexMatch, and the toy-dataset source, while removing works including GET3D, Magic3D, MVControl, and Gemma 3. It refines the distinction between reconstruction and learned completion and emphasizes depth/camera-pose limitations. The overall research positioning remains, despite the changed PointRefer attribution.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations, experimental discussion, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting and condensation. Method becomes Affostruction, Ablation study becomes Analysis, appendix prose is reorganized, and acknowledgments and revised author affiliations are added.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and A2 are redrawn. Three examples from v1 Figure A3 move into v2 Figure 3 with a heatmap legend; other older examples and the diversity panel disappear. v2 adds scene/failure figures and Table 4, relocates Table 3, and substantially rearranges figures and captions while retaining the ablation plots.

improvement.justification: v2 improves practical assessment through end-to-end runtime/memory measurements and explicit failure cases that qualify v1's optimistic interpretation of error propagation. Rewritten explanations and reorganized figures also help. These gains are limited by the new training-budget contradiction, inconsistent benchmark attribution, and removal of the direct same-query diversity demonstration while retaining multimodality claims. The core quantitative evidence is largely unchanged.
